# SMOD radiator transmission cooler failure

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

Send automatic transmission fluid to Blackstone Laboratories and check the lab report for coolant mixing. [t23]

[Partial] Inspect the ATF dipstick and coolant reservoir to check if both fluids appear old. [t27]

Replace the radiator if the vehicle has experienced an SMOD event. [t682]

[Partial] Check Nissan part numbers and inspect components for frothy contamination resembling strawberry milkshake. [t501]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. Send a sample of the automatic transmission fluid to Blackstone Laboratories for analysis.
2. Check the lab report specifically for signs that coolant has mixed into the oil.

_Procedure reported by [t23]._

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t682] [Partial]</summary>

1. Replace the radiator if the vehicle has experienced an SMOD event.
2. [Partial] Install an aftermarket unit after performing a cooling line bypass.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t501] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Check the Nissan part number stamped on top of the radiator to confirm if it is a known affected unit.
2. Inspect the overflow tank, radiator, and transmission fluid for signs of frothy contamination resembling strawberry milkshake.

</details>

## Parts

- [Partial] Aftermarket radiator [t682]
- [Partial] Cooling lines, bypass [t682]
- Radiator, check part number to avoid 'old' versions: Ensure it is not an older design version if replacing after initial repair [t24]

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Keep taking samples periodically to stay on top of the issue instead of immediately installing a bypass or new radiator. [t23]
- Check the radiator part number before installation to ensure it isn't an older design version that may have been on dealer shelves. [t24]
- [Partial] Perform a complete drain and fill of Matic S fluid after repair. [t24]
- [Partial] Perform a cooling line bypass before installing the new radiator. [t682]
- If part number matches an SMOD model but no symptoms exist, consider swapping the radiator or re-routing lines as a preventive measure. [t501]
- Note that bypassing the radiator may reduce cooling efficiency for those who tow or live in hot climates. [t501]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Installing an 'old' style radiator during initial repairs which leads to premature failure shortly thereafter. [t24]
